naat-sababi-00.png.sentence: Orange is a fruit whose taste is pleasant.

naat-sababi-01.png.sentence: I heard the man whose tone (of recitation) is beautiful.

naat-sababi-02.png.sentence: I lit a lamp whose light was strong (bright).

naat-sababi-03.png.sentence: I passed by a town whose residents were noble.

naat-sababi-04.png.sentence: Zaid scaled the tree whose trunk was thick.

naat-sababi-05.png.sentence: These are 2 men whose 2 uncles are scholars.

naat-sababi-06.png.sentence: You left the book whose pages were torn.

naat-sababi-07.png.sentence: I bought pens whose writing is beautiful.

naat-sababi-08.png.sentence: I travelled the sea whose fish is abundant.

naat-sababi-09.png.sentence: I entered a masjid whose doors were different.

naat-sababi-10.png.sentence:
يأتيني الرجلُ الضاربُ إبنُهُ زيدًا
The man whose son is hitting Zaid is coming.

naat-sababi-11.png.sentence:
رَأيتُ سيارةً فارغًا إطارَاها
I saw a car whose 2 tyres were flat.

naat-sababi-12.png.sentence:
زرتُ مدينةَ النبيِّ ﷺ النعيمَ جوُّهَا
I visited the city of the prophet ﷺ the atmosphere of which was pleasant.

naat-sababi-13.png.sentence:
إنّها بَقَرةٌ صَفْرَاءُ فَاقِعٌ لوْنُهَا
Indeed, it is a yellow cow whose colour is bright.

naat-sababi-14.png.sentence:
مررتُ بِالسيّاراتِ المكسورِ أبوابُهَا
I walked passed cars whose doors were broken.
